# Davy Keith

## Overview

- **Age:** 9 years old  <sub>[v3 c18 P9](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0009)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c8 P10](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0010)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolboy  <sub>[v2 c21 P0](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Davy is a fair, handsome little lad with a round head covered in fuzzy yellow ringlets. He has roguish, dancing hazel eyes, a snub nose, and a smile-filled mouth with a dimple in one cheek that gives him a comical, lopsided look when he laughs.

_Sources: [v2 c8 P25](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0025), [v2 c8 P33](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0033)_

## Personality

Davy is an energetic, mischievous, and highly inquisitive boy with an endless curiosity about the world around him. Though heedless, disobedient, and forgetful, he has a born knack for winning love and is deeply affectionate toward Anne. Practical in his outlook, he often lacks imagination, takes comfort in shared misfortunes, and rarely feels sorry for his misdeeds until after he has committed them.

_Sources: [v2 c8 P25](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0025), [v2 c8 P51](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0051), [v2 c16 P12](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0012), [v2 c18 P3](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0003), [v2 c24 P52](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0052)_

## History

Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned after their mother, Mary, passed away following a long illness. They were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables, where Davy quickly formed a strong attachment to Anne Shirley. Early in his stay, Davy engaged in frequent misbehavior, such as telling untruths, climbing forbidden shelves and falling onto lemon pies, and neglecting his prayers out of curiosity to see what would happen. After starting school, he sat with his friend Milty Boulter, with whom he competed regarding height and shared stories. Despite occasionally causing trouble—such as cutting up Dora's aprons, chasing Mrs. Lynde's rooster to death, and running away from Sunday School to go fishing with the Cottons—Davy gradually reformed under Anne and Marilla's guidance while retaining his lively inquisitiveness.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c8 P8](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0008), [v2 c8 P33](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0033), [v2 c10 P53](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0053), [v2 c10 P70](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0070), [v2 c17 P28](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0028), [v2 c21 P0](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0000), [v2 c26 P31](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0031), [v3 c5 P13](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0013), [v3 c5 P17](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0017), [v3 c13 P94](../source/v03-c13.md#nw-v03-c13-p0094), [v3 c40 P6](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0006)_

## Background by volume

- lost his father when he was a baby  <sub>[v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033)</sub>
- had no early bringing up due to his mother's prolonged illness  <sub>[v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033)</sub>
- associated with Mr. Sprott's children before moving to Green Gables  <sub>[v2 c7 P32](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0032), [v2 c10 P53](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0053)</sub>
- went without cake for a long time during his mother's illness  <sub>[v2 c8 P13](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0013)</sub>
- was scoured with hard soap by Mrs. Wiggins on his mother's funeral day  <sub>[v2 c8 P31](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0031)</sub>

## Quotes

> I didn’t hurt her much . . . she just cried ’cause she’s a girl. I’m glad I’m a boy but I’m sorry I’m a twin.  <sub>[v2 c8 P10](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0010)</sub>

> I’m going to be a storekeeper, like Mr. Blair, and keep heaps of candy and bananas.  <sub>[v2 c14 P31](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0031)</sub>

> I like Dora because she’s my sister but I like you because you’re you.  <sub>[v2 c19 P41](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0041)</sub>

> I run away from Sunday School—and went fishing with the Cottons—and I told ever so many whoppers to Mrs. Lynde—oh! ’most half a dozen—and—and—I—I said a swear word, Anne—a pretty near swear word, anyhow—and I called God names.  <sub>[v3 c13 P94](../source/v03-c13.md#nw-v03-c13-p0094)</sub>

> I mean to live to be a hundred years old, like Mr. Thomas Blewett of White Sands.  <sub>[v3 c14 P43](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0043)</sub>
